# cortex-ia — Full Context

cortex-ia is an OpenCode-only installer: a single Go binary that copies the
embedded workflow asset set into OpenCode's config root, manages MCP entries
inside the OpenCode config, and does both transactionally. It is not a
workflow scheduler and not a resident process — after a run, only files
exist. It configures OpenCode only and never writes anywhere else.

## Architecture

```
cmd/cortex-ia            main(): release version + internal/app
internal/app             CLI dispatch, flags, receipts, retired-surface guard
internal/tui             Bubble Tea TUI (Install/Sync, MCPs, Doctor/Recovery, Uninstall)
internal/install         Service facade: install, sync, doctor, rollback, uninstall, MCP ops
internal/pipeline        Plan/apply transaction: InstallV2, effects, journal, Rollback
internal/backup          Snapshots, manifests, verification, dedup, retention pruning
internal/mcpmanager      Managed MCP catalog, desired-entry validation, qualification, conflicts
internal/state           Installation metadata, lock, v2 agreement under ~/.cortex-ia/
internal/installmeta     MCP identity digests and install accreditation
internal/agents/opencode OpenCode native layout + pure asset mapping
internal/components/filemerge  JSONC decode/merge, atomic writes
internal/assets          go:embed runtime assets (config, AGENTS.md, agents, commands, skills, plugin)
```

`internal/app` owns no install, merge, or ownership logic: it parses intent,
delegates to `internal/install.Service`, and renders receipts. All ownership
decisions live in the service and its collaborators. The dispatcher fails
closed on retired surfaces via a preflight scan that stops at the `--`
verbatim separator.

## Asset mapping

`internal/agents/opencode/layout.go` is the single declaration of OpenCode's
native discovery surface (config, agents-doc, agent, command, skill, plugin).
`assetmap.go` maps embedded sources with `dest = path.Join(config root,
source)` validated against that one declaration. The mapping fails closed on
unsafe paths, kinds without a native destination (`_shared` contracts are
compile-time only), destinations off the native surface, and collisions —
including case-insensitive collisions on Windows and macOS.

## Transactional pipeline

`InstallV2` runs in three phases:

1. Plan — build the complete effect set plus conflict detection; dry-run and
   apply share this plan and a dry run writes nothing at all.
2. Backup — snapshot everything the apply phase may touch and verify it before
   any write. A failed verification aborts before any write.
3. Apply — write files atomically (temp file + rename), merge the config via
   `filemerge` (comments and user keys survive), journal the transaction,
   commit metadata + lock last. Any apply failure restores the pre-run state
   from that verified backup.

`internal/backup` also exports checksum-based dedup and retention-prune helpers,
but these helpers are not wired into the production Install/Sync/Rollback flow,
so the product currently does not promise automatic dedup/prune.

`sync` uses the same path and additionally plans removals for stale owned
artifacts from older versions.

## Managed MCP services

`install` registers the default managed selection: `cortex`
(`cortex mcp --tools=agent`) and `forgespec` (`npx -y forgespec-mcp`), both
native local servers. `context7` (`npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp`) is a
local catalog preset not selected by default; no preset ships a URL.
Custom servers are first-class via the typed `Desired` contract: a catalog
preset, a local exact command vector, or a remote URL, with `--env` and
`--header KEY=VALUE` assignments bound to exactly one kind each. Present
entries are qualified against recorded identity digests plus the secret-free
`mcpv2` full-postimage fingerprint (salt-keyed HMAC covering type, argv,
URL, env/header names and keyed value hashes, enabled, config path) and
reported as `managed`, `unmanaged-equivalent`, `conflict`, or `absent`;
conflict errors never contain secrets, legacy mcpv1-only records fail
closed for destructive accreditation (manual re-add remedy), and
`mcp list --json` is allow-listed to identity evidence only.

## CLI and TUI

```
cortex-ia                          Interactive TUI
cortex-ia install [--dry-run] [--overwrite]
cortex-ia sync [--dry-run] [--overwrite]
cortex-ia mcp add <name> (--preset | --local ... -- <cmd> | --remote <url>) [--dry-run]
cortex-ia mcp list [--json]
cortex-ia mcp remove <name> [--dry-run]
cortex-ia doctor
cortex-ia rollback [backup-id]
cortex-ia recover [list]        # read-only journal listing
cortex-ia recover <journal-id>  # typing the exact ID confirms recovery
cortex-ia uninstall [--dry-run]
cortex-ia version | help
```

## Safety rules

- Plan before write; `--dry-run` creates nothing, not even directories.
- Digest-bound confirmation: the real run re-plans with identical options
  and aborts with a typed stale-plan error on any drift before writing.
- One writer per home: every mutation holds a cross-process lock keyed by
  the canonical home (LockFileEx/flock) after confirmation; contention
  returns a typed busy result. Read-only commands never steal the lock.
- Fail-closed conflicts: unmanaged files at a managed destination abort the
  run; `--overwrite` must be given explicitly and confirmed on an
  interactive TTY after a verified backup.
- `rollback`, `recover`, `uninstall`, `mcp remove`, and `--overwrite`
  require an interactive terminal and an explicit confirmation; piped or
  closed input always fails closed.
- Rollback/recover restoration validates manifest containment, restores in
  reverse order under a journal, and reports success only after complete
  verified restoration; corrupt/foreign/drifted journals fail closed.
- `uninstall` removes only files whose digest matches the installation
  metadata; anything unverifiable or co-owned is retained and reported.

## Testing and gates

Persistent tests are deliberately scoped to the TUI (`internal/tui/`) and
simple existence/copy validation in `internal/pipeline/install_test.go`,
both against temporary homes. Deeper transactional oracles run as ephemeral
smokes and are deleted after execution. Full local gates, in hook order:
`gofmt -s -w .`, `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run ./...`,
`go test -count=1 ./...`.

Former multi-agent, persona, profile, model, skill-registry, and
SDD-compiler surfaces were removed and fail with an explicit
retired-surface error.
